attachments.origin_landmark: soleal line + posterior tibia; also fibular head/proximal fibula (fibula_l)
attachments.insertion_landmark: calcaneus (via Achilles tendon, joined by gastrocnemius)

actions: plantarflexes ankle (primary postural/gait plantarflexor -- crosses only the ankle, unlike gastrocnemius, so remains effective regardless of knee position)

functional_compartments.name: Single continuous multipennate mass (some studies describe faint superficial/deep compartment banding, not independently innervated)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: along the extensive central aponeurosis (soleus is a classically 'unipennate-to-multipennate' short-fiber, high-PCSA design specialized for sustained postural force)

functional_compartments.function_note: Largest PCSA of any lower-leg muscle -- short fascicles + very high pennation give enormous force at low shortening velocity, matched to its role as the primary antigravity/postural plantarflexor (slow-twitch dominant).
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)
